fullPassage: [1번] When you are successful and the new habit feels normal, it is time to create an anchor. The anchor is valuable for those situations in which you threaten to loose your new habit. I once created the habit of seeing beauty in every human being. So when I felt the habit was mine, I bought myself a geode, a stone that can be found around volcanoes. Geodes are rough on the outside but if you break them in two, inside there is a lovely cave filled with shining crystals. So I put the geode on my desk and after a year or so I had had a row with a person and I was really angry. I came into my office and threw my bag on the ground. "What a bad person!" I said out loud, and immediately my eye was drawn like a magnet to the geode and I realised that here I had a person with a very rough outside, but somewhere inside there must be something beautiful. [2번] Ellen Langer and her colleagues studied the conditions under which people engage in mindless conformity. To forty secretaries at a New York university, they sent a memo that said, "This paper is to be returned immediately to Room 238 through interoffice mail." Like almost all other memos at this university, this one was unsigned. Note that this is a pretty silly request; if the person who sent the memo wanted it, why did he or she send it in the first place? Langer and her colleagues hypothesized that secretaries would go ahead and return the memo without much thinking, because they would follow the norm that says, "Do what memos tell you to do." They were right; 90 percent of the secretaries dutifully returned the memo to Room 238. [3번] Many teachers' analogies are used to describe structural similarities. For instance, "a Molecule of Gas Is Like a Rubber Ball," "An Artery Is Like a Hose," and "Rock Strata Are Like Cake Layers." Teachers often assume that the students understand the sense in which these comparisons are made. In the first example, the teacher has in mind the idea that a gas molecule is elastic, and when it collides with another molecule or the wall of its container, it will rebound with about the same speed and energy that it had before the collision. Unless students have this relationship explained to them, some may understandably visualize the molecule as just a round object while others may think of it as a moving elastic sphere. That is, they may pay more attention to the analogy's structural attributes and too little attention to the interaction effects. [4번] Few people would dispute that in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, Europe and especially Great Britain dominated the world culturally, politically and economically. Britain was the crucible of the Industrial Revolution and its military forces secured the colonies as surely as the English language invaded their cultures. When Queen Victoria ascended to the throne in 1837, she presided over the largest empire in history: the empire on which the sun never set. If you had gone to her court in 1850 and suggested that this empire would be over within a generation, you would have been laughed out of the building. And yet it was true. By the end of World War I in 1918, the empire was fatally wounded and, by the time I was born in 1950, it was a memory.

✅ ① without much thinking: 본문 원문. follow the norm 맥락 + 90% 순응 결과와 일치
❌ ② through interoffice mail: 본문에 등장하지만 메모 발송 방식으로 빈칸과 무관한 정보
❌ ③ with careful deliberation: 신중한 고려 = mindless conformity의 반대
❌ ④ without detailed instructions: 세부 지시 없이 = 본문 주제와 다른 방향
det.tip: 'without much thinking'은 mindless conformity를 설명하는 핵심 표현. 비서들이 메모의 모순을 인식하지 못했다는 전후 맥락이 근거

questions.passage: Ellen Langer and her colleagues studied the ①<u>conditions</u> under which people engage in mindless conformity. To forty secretaries at a New York university, they sent a memo that said, "This paper is to be returned immediately to Room 238 through interoffice mail." Like almost all other memos at this university, this one was ②<u>verified</u>. Note that this is a pretty silly request; if the person who sent the memo wanted it, why did he or she send it in the first place? Langer and her colleagues hypothesized that secretaries would go ahead and return the memo without much thinking, because they would follow the ③<u>norm</u> that says, "Do what memos tell you to do." They were ④<u>right</u>; 90 percent of the secretaries dutifully returned the memo to Room 238.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① conditions=조건(맥락 적절), ② verified→unsigned 맞음(서명 없는이 맞음. verified=검증된은 부적절), ③ norm=규범(맥락 적절), ④ right=옳은/맞은(맥락 적절)
det.analysis:
❌ ① conditions: 'studied the conditions under which...' — 연구 맥락에 적절
✅ ② verified: 원문 'this one was unsigned(이 메모는 서명이 없었다)'. verified(검증된/확인된)으로 바꾸면 실험 설계 맥락에서 완전히 다른 의미
❌ ③ norm: 'follow the norm that says' — 사회 규범 맥락 적절
❌ ④ right: 'They were right' — '예측이 맞았다' 문맥 적절
det.tip: unsigned = 서명이 없는. verified = 검증된/확인된. 메모가 서명 없이 왔음에도 비서들이 따랐다는 실험 맥락에서 unsigned가 필수적

questions.passage: Many teachers' analogies are ①<u>used</u> to describe structural similarities. For instance, "a Molecule of Gas Is Like a Rubber Ball," "An Artery Is Like a Hose," and "Rock Strata Are Like Cake Layers." Teachers often ②<u>assume</u> that the students understand the sense in which these comparisons are made. In the first example, the teacher has in mind the idea that a gas molecule is elastic, and when it collides with another molecule or the wall of its container, it will ③<u>rebounding</u> with about the same speed and energy that it had before the collision. Unless students have this relationship ④<u>explained</u> to them, some may understandably visualize the molecule as just a round object while others may think of it as a moving elastic sphere. That is, they may pay more attention to the analogy's structural attributes and too little attention to the interaction effects.

❌ ① secured: 'its military forces secured the colonies' — 과거동사 정상
❌ ② ascended: 'Queen Victoria ascended to the throne in 1837' — 과거동사 정상
✅ ③ presiding(오류): 'she presided over the largest empire in history' — she가 주어이므로 본동사 presided 필요. presiding(현재분사)으로 바꾸면 절에 본동사 없어 오류
❌ ④ suggested: 'you had gone to her court and suggested' — had+과거분사 병렬 정상
det.tip: 주절 주어(she) 뒤에는 반드시 본동사 필요. 현재분사(presiding)는 본동사 역할 불가.

questions.passage: Few people would dispute that in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, Europe and especially Great Britain dominated the world ①<u>culturally</u>, politically and economically. Britain was the crucible of the Industrial Revolution and its military forces secured the colonies as surely as the English language invaded their cultures. When Queen Victoria ascended to the throne in 1837, she presided over the largest empire in history: the empire ②<u>on which</u> the sun never set. If you had gone to her court in 1850 and suggested that this empire would be over within a generation, you would have been ③<u>laughed</u> out of the building. And yet it was true. By the end of World War I in 1918, the empire was ④<u>fatal wounding</u> and, by the time I was born in 1950, it was a memory.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① culturally=문화적으로(부사), ② on which=전치사+관계대명사, ③ laughed=웃음거리가 됐을(수동태 과거분사), ④ fatally wounded→fatal wounding 오류(was 뒤 수동태 과거분사 필요)
det.analysis:
❌ ① culturally: 'dominated the world culturally, politically and economically' — 부사 병렬 정상
❌ ② on which: 'the empire on which the sun never set' — 전치사+관계대명사 정상
❌ ③ laughed: 'you would have been laughed out of the building' — 가정법과거완료 수동태 정상
✅ ④ fatal wounding(오류): 'the empire was fatally wounded' — was 뒤 수동태에는 과거분사(wounded) 필요. fatal wounding은 명사구로 was와 어법상 불가
det.tip: be + 과거분사 = 수동태. 'was fatally wounded'에서 fatally는 부사, wounded는 과거분사. 형용사+동명사 구조 불가.
